Note::tensor3¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

std::vector<Note> Note::tensor3() const

Preserve Three-Dimensional Cell Geometry¶

tensor3() decomposes an exactly rank-three Note into rank-two slab Notes. Unlike matrix(), it performs no rank promotion: scalar, vector, and matrix receivers reject even when they contain exactly one cell. Keeping each slab as a Note preserves dtype and its two-dimensional geometry.

For source shape [d0, d1, d2], result[i] has shape [d1, d2] and begins at source offset i * d1 * d2. Slabs share the source arena or aligned native lane buffer, so construction costs O(d0) and copies no cells. A slab owns its share of the backing allocation and safely outlives the source.

Zero extents are preserved exactly. For shape [2, 0, 3], the result contains two slab Notes, each with shape [0, 3]; the trailing extent remains available even though there are no rows or cells.

Example 1: Address Slabs, Rows, And Columns¶

const auto cube = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{
        "000", "001", "010", "011", "100", "101", "110", "111"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 3>{2, 2, 2});
const auto cells = cube.tensor3();

std::cout << "slab-shape=[" << cells[1].size(0) << ", "
          << cells[1].size(1) << "]"
          << " [1][0][1]=" << cells[1].at(1)
          << " [1][1][0]=" << cells[1].at(2) << '\n';

Output¶

slab-shape=[2, 2] [1][0][1]=101 [1][1][0]=110

Example 2: Preserve Empty Outer Structure¶

const auto cells = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 3>{2, 0, 3}).tensor3();

std::cout << "empty slabs=" << cells.size()
          << " rows=" << cells[0].size(0) << ',' << cells[1].size(0) << '\n';

Output¶

empty slabs=2 rows=0,0

Example 3: Lower Ranks Do Not Auto-Promote¶

try { (void)pluss::note::make({"x"}).tensor3(); }
catch (const pluss::Error&) { std::cout << "tensor3 rank1: rejected\n"; }

Output¶

tensor3 rank1: rejected

Call unsqueeze() or reshape({1, 1, 1}) explicitly when adding axes is part of the intended data model.

Example 4: Undefined Is Not An Empty Tensor¶

try { (void)pluss::Note::undefined().tensor3(); }
catch (const pluss::Error&) { std::cout << "tensor3 undefined: rejected\n"; }

Output¶

tensor3 undefined: rejected

See Also¶

  • matrix: preserve rank two and promote ranks zero or one.

  • vector: flatten all ranks in row-major order.

  • sizes_view: retain exact extents beside borrowed cells.

  • host: create an owning flat payload with explicit shape.
